title: How to Calculate Your Annual Salary from an Hourly Rate: 38-Hour Week, Fortnight, Tax, Super, and Novated Lease Salary Packaging
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes tax, super, fortnight pay, and novated lease salary packaging explained.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week over 52 weeks, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours, with super paid on top and tax deducted according to the 2026–27 resident rates.

faqs.q: How does a novated lease affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: A novated lease salary packaging arrangement lets you pay for a car lease and running costs from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. Because the Australian Taxation Office treats the lease as a salary sacrifice, your employer deducts the lease payments before calculating PAYG withholding. This lowers your annual taxable earnings, which can move you into a lower tax bracket and increase your fortnightly take-home pay. However, the exact benefit depends on your marginal tax rate, the lease amount, and any fringe benefits tax that may apply. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more details.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra payment on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. Under the Fair Work Commission’s National Minimum Wage, the casual loading is 25% of the base rate. For example, from 1 July 2026 the minimum base rate is $26.44 per hour, so a casual worker receives $33.05 per hour including loading. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check the box to add 25% casual loading to your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; always start with the base rate.

faqs.q: What are the 2026–27 tax brackets for residents?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 income year, the Australian Tax Office resident tax rates are: nil tax on the first $18,200; 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners. These rates apply to your annual gross salary after any salary sacrifice arrangements, such as a novated lease salary packaging. Our [reference tables](/data) provide more detail.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Annual Salary Calculation

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the standard way to estimate your annual gross pay is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees in Australia, the typical working week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Using 38 hours gives you a consistent benchmark for comparing job offers or planning your budget.

### The Formula in Practice

Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52

For a 38-hour week, that becomes:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 1,976 (since 38 × 52 = 1,976)

If your hourly rate is $30, your annual gross would be $30 × 1,976 = $59,280. This is the figure before tax, super, and any salary packaging arrangements like a novated lease salary packaging. Remember that super is paid on top of this amount by your employer, not deducted from it.

## Fortnightly Pay and the 52-Week Year

Many Australian employers pay their staff fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is your hourly rate times your weekly hours. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. This is useful for budgeting because most household bills are due monthly or fortnightly. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you understand award-specific pay cycles.

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It is important to know which rate applies to you. The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, giving a weekly minimum of $1,004.90. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making their minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave.

Award rates are higher than the minimum for many industries and occupations. They are set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and include specific classifications, penalty rates, and allowances. If you are covered by an award, your hourly rate must be at least the award rate for your classification. Casual loading is also applied on top of award rates. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into our [the timesheet](/); always start with the base rate and use the checkbox to add 25%.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is a compulsory contribution your employer must make into your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your salary. This means if your annual gross is $59,280, your employer contributes an extra $7,113.60 to super, provided your earnings do not exceed the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to your employer. When comparing job offers, always consider the total remuneration including super. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice arrangements like a novated lease salary packaging interact with super.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is your annual gross minus tax and the Medicare levy. The Australian Tax Office’s 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). Tax is calculated on your taxable income, which can be reduced by salary sacrifice arrangements such as a novated lease salary packaging. This can lower your tax bill and increase your fortnightly take-home pay. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator for a personalised calculation.

## Novated Lease Salary Packaging Explained

A novated lease salary packaging is an arrangement where your employer allows you to pay for a car lease and its running costs from your pre-tax salary. The lease payments are deducted from your gross salary before PAYG withholding is calculated, reducing your taxable income. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000 and you salary sacrifice $10,000 for a novated lease, your taxable income becomes $70,000, potentially lowering your marginal tax rate. The fortnightly lease payment is taken from your pay, but because it is pre-tax, the net cost to you is lower than if you paid after tax. This is a popular way to manage vehicle costs while optimising your tax position. Remember that fringe benefits tax may apply, and the arrangement must be documented with your employer. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page covers this in more detail.

## Using Our Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [the timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare levy, and super. The results are based on the 38-hour week and 52-week year, with the assumptions listed in the disclaimer. For more detailed information, visit our [reference tables](/data) which include tax brackets, super rates, and minimum wage figures. You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for industry averages from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, but remember these are averages, not medians for your specific job.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
